thread.title: Housing at Knowles Court to cost $5M
thread.title_full: Housing at Knowles Court to cost $5M

author: ohtadmin
title: Housing at Knowles Court to cost $5M
text:
Bringing affordable housing to the former ambulance barn would cost about $5 million, according to Eric Busch, managing partner of the Peregrine Group.
Busch and Erica Thornton, a designer and urban planner with Union Studio, presented a proposed 10-unit condominium plan to the town councilors at their July 20 meeting.
The area of the building would be 7,914 square feet with 3,274, 3,080 and 1,560 on the first, second and third floors, respectively. The units, including six two-bedroom and four one-bedroom condos, would range from 504 to 815 square feet.
There also would be a 300-square-foot office to serve as the headquarters for the harbor division.
“We looked to the design guidelines to stay consistent with what you would want to see in the district overall,” Thornton said. “Being a good neighbor to the street. Having frontage along the street, trying to create a nice public realm with sidewalks that connect to the street.”
The councilors unanimously endorsed a resolution to move the project forward to the planning commission for approval.
The town administrator, planning director and affordable housing committee “shall consider this resolution a directive to conclude pre-development considerations at 11 Knowles Court and solicit bids from affordable housing entities for development of new housing options specific to Jamestown’s households needs.”
The economics of the proposal, however, remain unclear.
Busch said if each unit sold for an average of $500,00, that would leave a gap of about $2.5 million to make up the difference of the construction cost due to the affordable units being subsidized.
The lower the income per residents, the more would need to be raised from other funding sources to meet that shortfall.
